analysis.answer: Under current law, abortion is prohibited after 15 weeks of gestation, with exceptions only to prevent the pregnant woman's death or serious permanent physical impairment. The measure removes this 15-week ban and permits abortion for any reason at any point prior to fetal viability.

Medical providers would be legally permitted to perform abortions between 15 weeks and viability, which may lead to an increase in the number of such procedures in the jurisdiction. Patients who previously would have had to travel out of state or carry the pregnancy to term would be able to obtain an abortion locally during this timeframe.
The measure addresses restrictions on abortion access after 15 weeks of pregnancy by extending the legal window for the procedure up to fetal viability.

Pregnant individuals gain the legal discretion to obtain an abortion between 15 weeks and fetal viability. Medical providers gain the ability to perform abortions during this period without needing to meet the medical emergency exceptions required under current law.
